chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed me, from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hussein ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, hates the wealthy oppressive person, the wicked old man, and the arrogant needy person. Then he said: Do you know who the arrogant needy person is? We said: He is one who has little wealth. He said: No, he is the one who does not draw closer to Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, with any of his wealth.
ai.seo_question: Who is the 'arrogant needy' person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the 'arrogant needy' (al-ṣaʿlūk al-mukhtāl) not by their lack of wealth, but by their failure to utilize whatever resources they possess for spiritual proximity to God. This highlights the Shia emphasis on *iḥtiṭāṭ* (spiritual preparedness) and the obligation of spending in charity, regardless of one's economic status, as a means of purifying the soul and demonstrating sincerity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-19 Hamzih ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Uthman, “Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, ‘

Indeed the Honorable the Exalted God is angry with the oppressive wealthy ones, wicked old men and the arrogant needy ones.’ Then the Imam (MGB) asked, ‘Do you know who the arrogant needy ones are?’ I said, ‘He is one who has little money.’ The Imam (MGB) said, ‘No. He is someone who would not spend any of his money in order to get closer to the Honorable the Exalted God.’”
